name: University of Cambridge
header:
University of Cambridge
United Kingdom · MASt Mathematics (Pure Mathematics / Part III); PhD Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics
Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Use 6 January for a funded application, not the later admission-only deadline.
• References are part of a complete application; an on-time form alone is insufficient.
• MASt funding is a separate competition and not a guarantee of later PhD admission.
• PhD page flags ATAS after an offer where applicable; MASt says no ATAS. Do not apply for ATAS before an
offer.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [2027 confirmed]
Conditionally eligible for MASt with a first-class-equivalent mathematics degree; US equivalence is normally
GPA 3.7/4.0. DPMMS PhD permits a comparable four-year mathematics degree, or three-year degree plus one
postgraduate year; a separate master's is not categorically mandatory. Advanced preparation and supervisor
fit remain competitive judgments. F-1 is not UK immigration permission. [c] [d] [m]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose the MASt pathway matching your background, or identify 2-3 suitable DPMMS supervisors and up to
two research areas. PhD informal contact with CV is encouraged but not mandatory. Secure referee consent;
upload documents and pay applicable fee before submitting. [j] [f] [h]
Adviser contact [2027 confirmed]
PhD informal email with brief research fit and CV is recommended; check the department's explicit 2027
availability table. It is not compulsory to secure a reply or commitment before applying. [j] [o]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Applicant Portal handles application, uploads, payment, and reference requests; Referee Portal receives
confidential references. Required uploads are PDFs under 2 MB, unencrypted; separate course applications
require separate documents and letters. [g] [f]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Both course-directory entries explicitly show Michaelmas 2027; departmental pages contain some old dates
beside new ones. [a] [b] [j] [l]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
MASt: 2 February 2027, 23:59 UK time. DPMMS PhD: 13 May 2027, 23:59 UK time, but contact
phd-admissions@maths.cam.ac.uk before submitting after 6 January. Late availability is not assured. [a] [b]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
Both routes: 6 January 2027, 23:59 UK time. Gates US-resident US-citizen round closed 14 October 2026; an
international F-1 student who is not a US citizen uses the later applicable round, not the US-citizen round. [a] [b]
[j]

Reference receipt [2027 confirmed]
All academic references must arrive by the relevant funding deadline (6 January 2027) for funding, or course
deadline for admission. An incomplete file is not considered. Gates reference must also meet its scholarship
deadline. [a] [b] [f]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
English proof normally follows an offer, by the offer-condition deadline; tests, if required, must be within two
years before course start. No GRE deadline is established because no GRE is listed for these courses. [e] [a] [b]
Supporting documents [2027 confirmed]
Supporting documents share the relevant course/funding deadline. MASt explicitly includes all documents and
references. Final academic evidence and other conditions are normally due 31 July for October start; follow
your offer. [b] [g] [n]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Acceptance deadline is stated in the individual offer certificate; 31 July is normally the conditions-completion
deadline, not a universal acceptance date. Scholarship acceptance can have a separate deadline. [n]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [2027 confirmed]
If testing is required: IELTS Academic total 7.0, listening/writing/speaking 7.0, reading 6.5; published TOEFL
scale total 100 with 25 each. Cambridge also lists C1/C2 alternatives. Verify accepted test format when
booking. [c] [d]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Inference from published exemption: a completed US bachelor's of at least three years, completed within two
years of Cambridge entry, normally removes the test requirement. UChicago should qualify on degree
location/duration; the portal and offer determine any condition. Nationality alone is not the basis. [e]
GRE General [Standing rule]
MASt explicitly does not require GRE. PhD does not list GRE; general Cambridge guidance says only send it
when the course requests it. No evidence that an unsolicited score helps. [l] [g] [a]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
No mathematics GRE is requested on either current course checklist. MASt explicitly states no GRE
requirement. Do not confuse non-required with a verified promise to consider optional scores. [l] [a]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [2027 confirmed]
Two references for each course application; academic referees are appropriate for a current undergraduate. [a]
[b] [f]

Scholarship references [Conflict]
Gates requires one additional reference focused on its scholarship criteria, and a PhD research proposal. The
same person may provide an academic and Gates reference, but they need different content. Check MASt
eligibility separately; the generic course-page Gates box is not proof of eligibility. [a] [q] [r]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Cambridge help says a portal invitation is sent automatically when the referee is nominated. Request referee
permission first; nomination can precede application submission. [p] [f]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations are not restricted to after submission. You may submit before letters arrive, but assessment waits
for them and the applicable deadline still controls. [f]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The Applicant Portal lets you manage reference requests and check submitted references; the MASt page
specifically instructs applicants to verify receipt there. [l] [f]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Before a referee submits, the applicant can change details or referee and send reminders, both before and
after submitting the application. A separate reference submission is required for each course. Public guidance
checked does not confirm replacement of an already-submitted letter. [f] [g]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [2027 confirmed]
Required CV upload for both. No public course-specific page limit found. General upload format: unencrypted
PDF under 2 MB. [a] [b] [g]
Statement of purpose [2027 confirmed]
Both require a portal response explaining reasons for applying, maximum 1,500 characters (prompt
paraphrase). No separate long SOP listed. [a] [b]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
No separate background/diversity essay is specified on either course checklist. Circumstances relevant to the
record can be explained through appropriate application sections; additional portal limits not publicly
established. [a] [b] [g]
Research-interest statement [2027 confirmed]
PhD: choose up to two research areas; proposed supervisors field 200 characters; project title 250 characters;
research summary 2,500 characters (paraphrase: areas/topics you intend to investigate). MASt has no
corresponding research-summary requirement listed. [a]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
Ordinary PhD admission asks for a short research summary, not a detailed project proposal. Gates PhD
applicants need a research proposal; its current exact length/format is unresolved because the funder's pages
could not be retrieved. [j] [a]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [2027 confirmed]
No mandatory writing sample, thesis, or uploaded paper appears on the two course checklists. PhD
research-experience response is optional, 2,500 characters. Unsolicited paper upload/link permissions
unverified. [a] [b]
Publications list [Standing rule]
No separate publications list specified publicly; CV is required. Whether the portal has a separate publication
field is unverified. [a] [b]

Course-list document [Standing rule]
A separate mathematics-course list or syllabus document is not specified for the ordinary UChicago applicant
on the public course checklists. Confirm any additional portal field; do not assume an extra upload is allowed.
[a] [b]
Scholarship essays [Conflict]
Gates application material needs independent confirmation: Cambridge's 2027 help still describes a
3,000-character (approximately 500-word) scholarship statement, while the Gates website was inaccessible in
this audit. Do not draft from this potentially stale prompt without checking the live funding section. Other
scholarships have their own prompts. [q]
Other short answers / materials [2027 confirmed]
No additional mandatory ordinary-course essay is listed. The optional PhD research-experience field is capped
at 2,500 characters. Uploads use the portal; there is no confirmed general right to substitute links for required
documents. [a] [g]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
No universal guaranteed annual mathematics stipend is published in the funding pages checked. Department
funding is competitive, can include research-council awards, and must not be treated as automatic. Obtain
exact maintenance amount, international fee coverage, and award period from each award. [k]
Years of support [Standing rule]
PhD course is 3-4 years; MASt nine months. This describes course duration, not a guaranteed funding term.
Scholarship-specific duration and summer support must be checked in the award. [a] [b] [k]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Funding consideration is available irrespective of fee status, but each award has separate eligibility.
Department explicitly expects applicants to seek other eligible awards. US residence on F-1 does not make one
eligible for US-citizen-only awards. [k] [j]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Funding is not guaranteed by admission. Confirm full overseas tuition coverage, maintenance, duration,
progress conditions, and any nationality restriction in the actual award. [k]
Extra funding application [2027 confirmed]
Complete the funding section by 6 January; Gates adds its own reference/proposal/materials. MASt department
lists several awards, some automatic and others requiring an expression of interest; read each scheme. [a] [b]
[l]
Other funding routes [Conflict]
Cambridge Trust, college awards, departmental/research-council support, G-Research studentship (PhD), and
Gates (eligible PhD courses) are routes to investigate. MASt page also lists Trinity studentship and Squarepoint
partial maintenance awards. Some text still names 2026 dates: confirm current scheme particulars. [j] [l]
Application fee [Standing rule]
PhD: GBP 20 per applicant per entry year, covering up to seven doctoral applications. MASt: GBP 85 per
application. Pay online before submission; Visa/Mastercard accepted, not AmEx. [h]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
International automatic waiver requires both nationality of an eligible listed country and residence there since
birth, with limited displacement exceptions. Other international requests are refused; no UChicago/F-1 waiver
is provided. UK/refugee routes have separate tests and lead times. If eligible for January-funding waiver route,
published request date is 11 December 2026; do not pay first. [i]

text:
University of Cambridge
United Kingdom · MASt Mathematics (Pure Mathematics / Part III); PhD Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics
Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Use 6 January for a funded application, not the later admission-only deadline.
• References are part of a complete application; an on-time form alone is insufficient.
• MASt funding is a separate competition and not a guarantee of later PhD admission.
• PhD page flags ATAS after an offer where applicable; MASt says no ATAS. Do not apply for ATAS before an
offer.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [2027 confirmed]
Conditionally eligible for MASt with a first-class-equivalent mathematics degree; US equivalence is normally
GPA 3.7/4.0. DPMMS PhD permits a comparable four-year mathematics degree, or three-year degree plus one
postgraduate year; a separate master's is not categorically mandatory. Advanced preparation and supervisor
fit remain competitive judgments. F-1 is not UK immigration permission. [c] [d] [m]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose the MASt pathway matching your background, or identify 2-3 suitable DPMMS supervisors and up to
two research areas. PhD informal contact with CV is encouraged but not mandatory. Secure referee consent;
upload documents and pay applicable fee before submitting. [j] [f] [h]
Adviser contact [2027 confirmed]
PhD informal email with brief research fit and CV is recommended; check the department's explicit 2027
availability table. It is not compulsory to secure a reply or commitment before applying. [j] [o]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Applicant Portal handles application, uploads, payment, and reference requests; Referee Portal receives
confidential references. Required uploads are PDFs under 2 MB, unencrypted; separate course applications
require separate documents and letters. [g] [f]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Both course-directory entries explicitly show Michaelmas 2027; departmental pages contain some old dates
beside new ones. [a] [b] [j] [l]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
MASt: 2 February 2027, 23:59 UK time. DPMMS PhD: 13 May 2027, 23:59 UK time, but contact
phd-admissions@maths.cam.ac.uk before submitting after 6 January. Late availability is not assured. [a] [b]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
Both routes: 6 January 2027, 23:59 UK time. Gates US-resident US-citizen round closed 14 October 2026; an
international F-1 student who is not a US citizen uses the later applicable round, not the US-citizen round. [a] [b]
[j]

Reference receipt [2027 confirmed]
All academic references must arrive by the relevant funding deadline (6 January 2027) for funding, or course
deadline for admission. An incomplete file is not considered. Gates reference must also meet its scholarship
deadline. [a] [b] [f]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
English proof normally follows an offer, by the offer-condition deadline; tests, if required, must be within two
years before course start. No GRE deadline is established because no GRE is listed for these courses. [e] [a] [b]
Supporting documents [2027 confirmed]
Supporting documents share the relevant course/funding deadline. MASt explicitly includes all documents and
references. Final academic evidence and other conditions are normally due 31 July for October start; follow
your offer. [b] [g] [n]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Acceptance deadline is stated in the individual offer certificate; 31 July is normally the conditions-completion
deadline, not a universal acceptance date. Scholarship acceptance can have a separate deadline. [n]
English and GRE
English requirement [2027 confirmed]
If testing is required: IELTS Academic total 7.0, listening/writing/speaking 7.0, reading 6.5; published TOEFL
scale total 100 with 25 each. Cambridge also lists C1/C2 alternatives. Verify accepted test format when
booking. [c] [d]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Inference from published exemption: a completed US bachelor's of at least three years, completed within two
years of Cambridge entry, normally removes the test requirement. UChicago should qualify on degree
location/duration; the portal and offer determine any condition. Nationality alone is not the basis. [e]
GRE General [Standing rule]
MASt explicitly does not require GRE. PhD does not list GRE; general Cambridge guidance says only send it
when the course requests it. No evidence that an unsolicited score helps. [l] [g] [a]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
No mathematics GRE is requested on either current course checklist. MASt explicitly states no GRE
requirement. Do not confuse non-required with a verified promise to consider optional scores. [l] [a]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload transcripts/certificates for degree studies; interim or unofficial transcript accepted while studying. Final
authentic documents may be required after offer. Non-English records need registered-translator English
translation. PDF, under 2 MB, unencrypted. [g]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
A separate mathematics-course list or syllabus document is not specified for the ordinary UChicago applicant
on the public course checklists. Confirm any additional portal field; do not assume an extra upload is allowed.
[a] [b]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [2027 confirmed]
Two references for each course application; academic referees are appropriate for a current undergraduate. [a]
[b] [f]

Scholarship references [Conflict]
Gates requires one additional reference focused on its scholarship criteria, and a PhD research proposal. The
same person may provide an academic and Gates reference, but they need different content. Check MASt
eligibility separately; the generic course-page Gates box is not proof of eligibility. [a] [q] [r]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Cambridge help says a portal invitation is sent automatically when the referee is nominated. Request referee
permission first; nomination can precede application submission. [p] [f]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations are not restricted to after submission. You may submit before letters arrive, but assessment waits
for them and the applicable deadline still controls. [f]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The Applicant Portal lets you manage reference requests and check submitted references; the MASt page
specifically instructs applicants to verify receipt there. [l] [f]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Before a referee submits, the applicant can change details or referee and send reminders, both before and
after submitting the application. A separate reference submission is required for each course. Public guidance
checked does not confirm replacement of an already-submitted letter. [f] [g]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [2027 confirmed]
Required CV upload for both. No public course-specific page limit found. General upload format: unencrypted
PDF under 2 MB. [a] [b] [g]
Statement of purpose [2027 confirmed]
Both require a portal response explaining reasons for applying, maximum 1,500 characters (prompt
paraphrase). No separate long SOP listed. [a] [b]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
No separate background/diversity essay is specified on either course checklist. Circumstances relevant to the
record can be explained through appropriate application sections; additional portal limits not publicly
established. [a] [b] [g]
Research-interest statement [2027 confirmed]
PhD: choose up to two research areas; proposed supervisors field 200 characters; project title 250 characters;
research summary 2,500 characters (paraphrase: areas/topics you intend to investigate). MASt has no
corresponding research-summary requirement listed. [a]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
Ordinary PhD admission asks for a short research summary, not a detailed project proposal. Gates PhD
applicants need a research proposal; its current exact length/format is unresolved because the funder's pages
could not be retrieved. [j] [a]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [2027 confirmed]
No mandatory writing sample, thesis, or uploaded paper appears on the two course checklists. PhD
research-experience response is optional, 2,500 characters. Unsolicited paper upload/link permissions
unverified. [a] [b]
Publications list [Standing rule]
No separate publications list specified publicly; CV is required. Whether the portal has a separate publication
field is unverified. [a] [b]

Course-list document [Standing rule]
A separate mathematics-course list or syllabus document is not specified for the ordinary UChicago applicant
on the public course checklists. Confirm any additional portal field; do not assume an extra upload is allowed.
[a] [b]
Scholarship essays [Conflict]
Gates application material needs independent confirmation: Cambridge's 2027 help still describes a
3,000-character (approximately 500-word) scholarship statement, while the Gates website was inaccessible in
this audit. Do not draft from this potentially stale prompt without checking the live funding section. Other
scholarships have their own prompts. [q]
Other short answers / materials [2027 confirmed]
No additional mandatory ordinary-course essay is listed. The optional PhD research-experience field is capped
at 2,500 characters. Uploads use the portal; there is no confirmed general right to substitute links for required
documents. [a] [g]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
No universal guaranteed annual mathematics stipend is published in the funding pages checked. Department
funding is competitive, can include research-council awards, and must not be treated as automatic. Obtain
exact maintenance amount, international fee coverage, and award period from each award. [k]
Years of support [Standing rule]
PhD course is 3-4 years; MASt nine months. This describes course duration, not a guaranteed funding term.
Scholarship-specific duration and summer support must be checked in the award. [a] [b] [k]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Funding consideration is available irrespective of fee status, but each award has separate eligibility.
Department explicitly expects applicants to seek other eligible awards. US residence on F-1 does not make one
eligible for US-citizen-only awards. [k] [j]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Funding is not guaranteed by admission. Confirm full overseas tuition coverage, maintenance, duration,
progress conditions, and any nationality restriction in the actual award. [k]
Extra funding application [2027 confirmed]
Complete the funding section by 6 January; Gates adds its own reference/proposal/materials. MASt department
lists several awards, some automatic and others requiring an expression of interest; read each scheme. [a] [b]
[l]
Other funding routes [Conflict]
Cambridge Trust, college awards, departmental/research-council support, G-Research studentship (PhD), and
Gates (eligible PhD courses) are routes to investigate. MASt page also lists Trinity studentship and Squarepoint
partial maintenance awards. Some text still names 2026 dates: confirm current scheme particulars. [j] [l]
Application fee [Standing rule]
PhD: GBP 20 per applicant per entry year, covering up to seven doctoral applications. MASt: GBP 85 per
application. Pay online before submission; Visa/Mastercard accepted, not AmEx. [h]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
International automatic waiver requires both nationality of an eligible listed country and residence there since
birth, with limited displacement exceptions. Other international requests are refused; no UChicago/F-1 waiver
is provided. UK/refugee routes have separate tests and lead times. If eligible for January-funding waiver route,
published request date is 11 December 2026; do not pay first. [i]

Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
MASt page has generic Gates material although institutional fellowship guidance excludes MASt; verify directly
before relying on Gates. Squarepoint text still says 6 January 2026, alongside the 2027 main deadline. Gates
prompt wording in Cambridge help may be stale. These are unresolved rather than silently corrected. [b] [l] [q]
[r]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Check current Gates eligibility/prompt directly; ask about 2027 stipend and full overseas-fee coverage; verify
any course-list upload and already-submitted letter replacement. Confirm supervisor availability before
outreach. Grojnowski's official list has no recent paper, so recent activity cannot be assessed from that list
alone. [o] [k]
